model_annotations.Bulgarian: Диаграмата илюстрира зависимостта между перплекситета и процентната стойност на разреденост (Sparsity Rate) за два различни подхода: Per-Output и Per-Layer, представени като групирани стълбове. Хоризонталната ос (абсциса) показва стойностите на разредеността, изразени като проценти, и включва значения от 10% до 80% с интервал от 10%, като категориите са подредени по низходящ ред. Вертикалната ос (ордината) представлява перплекситета и е използвана логаритмична скала, като етикетът е "Perplexity", а стойностите са от 10⁰ (1) до 10³ (1000), със стандартни логаритмични интервали. Всеки процентен клас на разреденост съдържа два стълба – синьо за Per-Output и оранжево за Per-Layer, които показват съответните стойности на перплекситета. Стойностите на перплекситета са ниски за разредености до 50%, като синият стълб е по-нисък от оранжевия. От 60% нататък, стойностите на перплекситета растат, като оранжевият стълб за Per-Layer е по-висок от синия за Per-Output във всички класове от 60% до 80%. При 80% разреденост, перплекситетът за Per-Layer достига най-високата стойност, близка до 10³, докато за Per-Output е малко по-ниска, около 10². Диаграмата включва легенда в горния ляв ъгъл, която свързва цветовете на стълбовете със съответните подходи.
model_annotations.Chinese: The bar chart compares the perplexity of two models, Per-Output and Per-Layer, across different sparsity rates ranging from 10% to 80%. The horizontal axis represents the sparsity rate, with categories labeled as 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, and 80%, arranged in ascending order. The vertical axis, labeled "Perplexity," uses a logarithmic scale with values ranging from 10^0 (1) to 10^3 (1000), marked at intervals of 10^1 (10), 10^2 (100), and 10^3 (1000). For each sparsity rate, two bars are displayed side-by-side: a blue bar representing the Per-Output model and an orange bar representing the Per-Layer model. At sparsity rates of 10% through 50%, both models exhibit low perplexity values, with the Per-Output model's perplexity being slightly higher than the Per-Layer model's, both remaining below 10. At 60% sparsity, the perplexity for both models increases, with the Per-Output model reaching approximately 10 and the Per-Layer model reaching approximately 15. At 70% sparsity, the perplexity continues to rise, with the Per-Output model at approximately 30 and the Per-Layer model at approximately 60. At 80% sparsity, the perplexity for both models increases significantly, with the Per-Output model reaching approximately 500 and the Per-Layer model reaching approximately 800, the latter being the highest value observed in the chart. The legend in the top-left corner identifies the blue bars as "Per-Output" and the orange bars as "Per-Layer."
model_annotations.English: The bar chart illustrates the relationship between sparsity rate and perplexity for two different configurations, "Per-Output" and "Per-Layer," with the y-axis representing perplexity on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^0 to 10^3 and the x-axis showing sparsity rate from 10% to 80%. For each sparsity rate, two bars are presented: a blue bar for "Per-Output" and an orange bar for "Per-Layer." At sparsity rates of 10%, 20%, and 30%, the perplexity values for both configurations are low and nearly identical, with both bars reaching approximately 10^0.5. At 40% sparsity, the perplexity increases slightly for both, with "Per-Output" at about 10^0.7 and "Per-Layer" at approximately 10^0.8. At 50%, the values continue to rise, with "Per-Output" at around 10^0.8 and "Per-Layer" at about 10^0.9. At 60%, the perplexity for both configurations increases significantly, with "Per-Output" at approximately 10^1.2 and "Per-Layer" at around 10^1.3. At 70%, the perplexity values continue to climb, with "Per-Output" at about 10^1.5 and "Per-Layer" at approximately 10^1.7. At 80% sparsity, the perplexity reaches its peak, with "Per-Output" at around 10^2.2 and "Per-Layer" at approximately 10^2.4, indicating that "Per-Layer" consistently has a higher perplexity than "Per-Output" across all sparsity rates.
model_annotations.German: Das Balkendiagramm visualisiert die Beziehung zwischen der Sparsitätsrate und der Komplexität, wobei die Komplexität auf einer logarithmischen Skala in der vertikalen Achse dargestellt ist und die Sparsitätsrate in Prozent auf der horizontalen Achse angegeben ist. Die horizontale Achse zeigt Sparsitätsraten von 10% bis 80% in 10%-Schritten, wobei die Kategorien in aufsteigender Reihenfolge angeordnet sind. Die vertikale Achse, beschriftet mit „Perplexity“, reicht von 10⁰ bis 10³ und verwendet eine logarithmische Skala. Zwei verschiedene Messgrößen, „Per-Output“ und „Per-Layer“, sind durch farbige Balken repräsentiert: „Per-Output“ ist durch einen blauen Balken und „Per-Layer“ durch einen orangefarbenen Balken dargestellt. Für jede Sparsitätsrate sind zwei nebeneinander stehende Balken angeordnet, wobei die Gruppierung nach Sparsitätsrate erfolgt. Die Balkenlängen variieren mit der Sparsitätsrate: bei 10% und 20% sind die Balken sehr kurz, bei 30% und 40% leicht erhöht, bei 50% und 60% weiter ansteigend, bei 70% deutlich höher und bei 80% am höchsten. Bei 80% erreichen sowohl der blaue als auch der orangefarbene Balken Werte nahe 10³, wobei der orangefarbene Balken leicht höher ist. Die Balken sind nicht hervorgehoben oder durch zusätzliche visuelle Elemente gekennzeichnet.
